newsitem.title: USA: Fulton County, Ga., approves basketball arena.
newsitem.headline: Fulton County, Ga., approves basketball arena.

text.p: Georgia's Fulton County Commission approved a revised agreement to build a $213 millon arena for the Atlanta Hawks basketball team by a 5-2 vote Wednesday, the commission clerk said.
The vote was the final hurdle for the arena project, which previously was approved by the Atlanta City Council and the Atlanta-Fulton Recreation Authority.
The agreement calls for the authority to issue $140 million of revenue bonds to finance construction of the 20,000-seat arena, with the Hawks' paying debt service on the bonds.

Under the original agreement, the Hawks' pledged all team revenues to repay the bonds. The deal had to be revised because National Basketball Association rules require that player salaries take precedence over other obligations.
Under the revised plan, the team itself is pledged as collateral, and could be sold to repay the debt if arena revenues are inadequate.

The arena approval is expected to bolster Atlanta's bid for a National Hockey League expansion team. League officials are meeting in New York and are expected to announce in a few days which of six cities it will recommend for a new team.
The Hawks' owner, the Turner Broadcasting System TBSa.A, has bid for a hockey franchise.
